title: A surjection is the coequalizer of any epimorphic kernel-pair cover
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $p:\mathcal P\to\mathcal F$ be an epimorphism of sheaves of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $K=\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal F}\mathcal P$ with projections $r,s:K\rightrightarrows\mathcal P$, and let $e:R\to K$ be an epimorphism. Then $(\mathcal F,p)$ is a coequalizer of the composite pair $r\circ e,s\circ e:R\rightrightarrows\mathcal P$ in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 0CAI (lemma-filtered-colimit-constructibles), proof at lines 3038-3046: apply Lemma 0CAH to the fibre product and use the resulting surjection to present F as a coequalizer

proof.text: *Step 1 (the setting).* The sheaves of sets on $X$ are the sheaves of sets on the site $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ (objects the open subsets of $X$, morphisms the inclusions, coverings the open covers $\{U_i\subseteq U\}$ with $\bigcup_iU_i=U$), a site in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1), with $U_i\times_UU_j=U_i\cap U_j$; the category of sheaves of sets on $X$ is $\Sh(\operatorname{Opens}(X))$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] the fibre product $K=\mathcal P\times_{\mathcal F}\mathcal P$ exists in this category, is given by $K(U)=\{(a,b)\in\mathcal P(U)^2: p_U(a)=p_U(b)\}$ with $r,s$ the two projections, and has the universal property of a fibre product of $p$ with itself: $p\circ r=p\circ s$, and for morphisms $a,b:\mathcal T\to\mathcal P$ of sheaves with $p\circ a=p\circ b$ there is exactly one $c:\mathcal T\to K$ with $r\circ c=a$, $s\circ c=b$.

*Step 2 (the kernel pair).* Since $p$ is an epimorphism of $\Sh(\operatorname{Opens}(X))$ and $(K,r,s)$ is a fibre product of $p$ with itself (Step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-kernel-pair-coequalizer] applied to the site $\operatorname{Opens}(X)$ shows that $(\mathcal F,p)$ is a coequalizer of $r,s:K\rightrightarrows\mathcal P$: for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ and every $q:\mathcal P\to\mathcal G$ with $q\circ r=q\circ s$ there is exactly one $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ with $u\circ p=q$.

*Step 3 (precomposition with the epimorphism $e$).* First $p\circ(r\circ e)=(p\circ r)\circ e=(p\circ s)\circ e=p\circ(s\circ e)$, so $(\mathcal F,p)$ is a cocone on the pair $r\circ e,s\circ e$. Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets and $q:\mathcal P\to\mathcal G$ with $q\circ r\circ e=q\circ s\circ e$, i.e. $(q\circ r)\circ e=(q\circ s)\circ e$. Since $e:R\to K$ is an epimorphism, $q\circ r=q\circ s$. By Step 2 there is exactly one $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ with $u\circ p=q$. Thus every morphism $q$ equalizing $r\circ e,s\circ e$ factors uniquely through $p$; since a cocone on the parallel pair $R\rightrightarrows\mathcal P$ is determined by its component on $\mathcal P$ (the component on $R$ being $q\circ r\circ e$), this is the statement that $(\mathcal F,p)$ is a colimit of the diagram $r\circ e,s\circ e:R\rightrightarrows\mathcal P$, i.e. a coequalizer, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
